source_annotations.explanation: The fourth glyph of XAX?F is overstruck/indeterminate. This question mark is a transcription placeholder for one visible source slot, not a printed question mark and not an unprinted insertion. It is independently distinct from the printed dash at109.
The G is faded but its lower-right bar survives. Primary transcription accepts G; the separate masked sensitivity variant leaves the resulting initial code character unresolved.
The final A of XXGVA is faint. Primary transcription accepts A; the separate masked sensitivity variant leaves the resulting E in ABGESANDT unresolved.
The source visibly spaces this group as XAA VF; the internal space contributes no coordinate and all five visible letters remain.

prior_attribution_check.key_credit: Unchanged published Nov4–6 key with original provenance.

limits: The Karl Michael and grand-duke references are what this source says; no independent biographical identification or confirmation of delivery/reply is asserted.
The literal ABGESANDT immediately before HANDSCHREIBEN lacks the adjective ending E expected in normal German. No extra plaintext character is inserted. The later repeated ABGESANDT is also retained.
BXMXK, references32982XBX2 and GX4774XROEMX1, and every numeral/letter label remain literal.
The seaplane order says what to do with any personnel returned; it does not prove a transfer occurred.
All three bodies were previously present in a repository screen. No historical first-solution claim is made.
There is no source insertion, deletion, length change or key change. Exact re-encryption verifies the declared editorial operations, not historical uniqueness.
